cards.hint: Think about the minimum share for a new savings program.
options: at least 10 percent of earnings
about 5 percent of earnings
six to nine percent of earnings
cards.quote: help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.
cards.stem: What share of earnings should go directly to savings after steady work begins

cards.hint: Recall how many months of costs cover an emergency.
options: at least three months’ worth of living expenses
at least 10 percent of what you earn
six to nine months’ worth of living expenses
cards.quote: have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.
cards.stem: What emergency cushion is described as a good rule to live by

cards.hint: Think about the higher range mentioned for extra safety.
options: six to nine months’ worth of living expenses
at least three months’ worth of living expenses
at least 10 percent of earnings
cards.quote: it’s better to have more savings—like six to nine months’ worth of living expenses, instead of only three.
cards.stem: If possible, what larger cushion is described as better than only three

cards.hint: Think about the safe place mentioned for keeping money.
options: a federally insured bank or credit union
credit cards or loan options that charge a high interest rate
a retirement account at work called a 401(k)
cards.quote: Talk about how to keep money in a safe place, like a federally insured bank or credit union.
cards.stem: Where should emergency money be kept for safety
